args.description: Full-body game character reference of the deer from the reference image, front view, facing the camera. The reference shows no deer: it is only the dark pine forest edge whose palette and evening light the deer must match; draw one deer and nothing else, no trees, no figures. Same design exactly: slender red deer doe with a warm russet-brown coat, a paler fawn belly, throat and inner legs, a cream rump patch and short white-edged tail, large dark eyes, big upright ears, a dark wet nose, thin legs with small dark hooves, no antlers. Seen exactly from the front, not three-quarter like a deer standing side-on: like looking at a deer walking straight at you, its head points straight at the camera with both of its eyes and both ears equally visible, and the face, neck and chest are square and symmetric about the image's vertical centre line. Only the front of the face, the throat and the chest show; the body is completely hidden straight behind the chest. The two front legs stand side by side, symmetric, and the two hind legs only just peek out behind them. Match the rendering style of the second reference image exactly: the same chunky voxel pixel-art look, block size, outline-free shading and soft lighting, but not its design. Whole animal from the tips of its ears down to its hooves, standing square on all four hooves in a neutral alert pose, head level, short tail held down, nothing cropped; the spine points exactly along the view direction, so in a front or back view the body is foreshortened straight behind the head with the two front legs side by side and symmetric, not turned three-quarter, and in a profile view the spine runs exactly sideways. Plain flat white background, no floor, no shadow, no text, no other figures. One single view only, not a sheet of several views.

args.prompt: Game character turnaround reference. The deer stands perfectly still in a neutral idle pose on an invisible turntable and rotates a full 360 degrees at a constant speed, turning to show its left side, then its back, then its right side, then front again. Locked-off camera, slightly elevated looking down, no camera movement, no zoom, no perspective change. Plain flat white background, even soft lighting. The design stays exactly identical: slender red deer doe with a warm russet-brown coat, a paler fawn belly, throat and inner legs, a cream rump patch and short white-edged tail, large dark eyes, big upright ears, a dark wet nose, thin legs with small dark hooves, no antlers, standing on all four hooves. No flashing, glowing or pulsing light: every colour keeps exactly the same brightness in every frame. Crisp sharp detail in every frame, no motion blur, no ghosting, no walking, no text.

Game sprite walk cycle. The deer walks in place on a treadmill, keeping exactly the facing direction of the first frame (facing the camera). Holding exactly the body angle of the first frame: torso does not twist. Calm steady deer walk on the spot, one full stride a second: legs lifting high and delicately in turn, all four legs clearly alternating, back level, head held up and level, slight body bob; its body never moves forward. The deer stays exactly centered, does not turn, move or change size. Locked-off camera, no zoom, plain flat white background, even lighting, crisp frames, no motion blur. Two full steps, loops seamlessly back to the starting pose.

Game sprite attack. The deer keeps exactly the facing direction of the first frame (facing the camera) and the body angle of the first frame: torso does not twist away. In one quick motion it lowers its head and neck down to graze the grass right at its front hooves, nibbling, then lifts its head back up to the start pose; all four hooves stay planted on the same spot, then returns exactly to the starting pose and holds it for the last frames. The deer stays exactly centered, feet stay planted, no turning, no change of size. No flashing, glowing or pulsing light: every colour keeps exactly the same brightness in every frame. Locked-off camera, no zoom, plain flat white background, even lighting, crisp frames, no motion blur, no speed lines, no effects.

Game sprite death. The deer starts exactly in the pose and facing of the first frame (facing the camera). It is struck down where it stands: all four hooves stay planted on the ground line until the legs fold, it does not rear, hop, jump, lift its front legs or rise up at any moment; its front knees buckle first so its chest drops straight down, then its hind legs fold and it sinks onto its belly and then rolls onto its side on the exact spot where it stood, head resting on the ground, legs stretched out; it only ever moves downward. It lies still on the ground for the last half second. The body stays centered on the same spot and does not slide out of frame. No flashing, glowing or pulsing light: every colour keeps exactly the same brightness in every frame. No blood, no gore, no fading, no particles, no effects. Locked-off camera, no zoom, plain flat white background, even lighting, crisp frames, no motion blur.
